name: Prehistoric Rock Art Sites in the Côa Valley and Siega Verde
description: Along the banks of the Côa in Portugal and the Águeda in Spain, riverside rock faces are covered with engraved animals made by Ice Age hunters. Around 5,000 figures are scattered across Foz Côa and about 440 at Siega Verde, many of them horses, aurochs and deer. Unlike the famous painted caves, these galleries lie open to the sky, where visitors can see them in the landscape that inspired them.
